name: June of 44
label: Quarterstick
lede: Four people from four cities and four bands cut a record in Brooklyn in four days, then spent five years turning a math-rock template into dub, strings and fifteen-minute closers.

eras.title: Four bands, one name
eras.text: Rodan is over, Codeine is over, and four people spread across four cities decide to make a record anyway. It's written fast and recorded in Brooklyn in four days.

years.src: POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller · Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years · Wikipedia: June of 44
years.h: [[Rodan|1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd]]'s guitarist starts a band with three people from three other bands
years.p: Jeff Mueller brings Rodan's angles, Fred Erskine brings [[Hoover|d691df14-6955-4cae-9dcc-318fb7d75984]]'s bass and trumpet, Doug Scharin brings drums from Rex, and Sean Meadows (also of [[Lungfish|5af88bca-9c13-424a-b63c-b5c96c69cb0e]]) brings a second guitar.
years.xp:
The four had met on tour in 1992 and 1993. They came together formally in November 1994, and they lived nowhere near each other: Mueller bounced between Chicago, Louisville and New York, Meadows was in Baltimore, Scharin in Williamsburg, Erskine in Washington, D.C. Mueller recalls it moving so fast that nobody could tell if the music was any good.

Mueller has described the idea as four people gathering for a few weeks to make a record and then sailing off in other directions. It turned into five years.

years.src: Wikipedia: June of 44 · POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller
years.h: Named for a pile of letters between Henry Miller and Anaïs Nin
years.p: The band took its name from the correspondence between the two writers.
years.xp: The nautical theme that runs through the first three records was Mueller's own project rather than a group decision, he says. He also stamped it on the objects: he printed the first record's packaging on his own letterpress, his first printing job.

years.src: Wikipedia: Engine Takes to the Water · Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years · POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller · AllMusic: June of 44 Biography
years.h: Engine Takes to the Water · Quarterstick QS32
years.p: Eight songs recorded in four days in mid-December 1994 at Plantain Recording House in Brooklyn, with [[James Murphy|6b70c46c-5c83-4cc7-99c1-e76b68919c6a]] behind the board.
years.xp: Murphy, later the founder of [[LCD Soundsystem|2aaf7396-6ab8-40f3-9776-a41c42c8e26b]], recorded it. It came out on Quarterstick on CD, cassette and LP, the same label that had put out Rodan's Rusty the year before. AllMusic hears the angular riffs, extreme dynamics and shifting meters of Rodan, with more room around them.

eras.title: Sailing orders
eras.text: Bob Weston takes over the board, the songs get longer, and the side projects start piling up. Mueller starts a second band before the first has made its third record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tropics and Meridians · POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller · Wikipedia: Rodan (band)
years.h: Tropics and Meridians opens with nine minutes of "Anisette"
years.p: Six songs, 36 minutes, recorded in Chicago with [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]] producing. Quarterstick QS44.
years.xp:
Weston, who had produced Rodan's Rusty, would stay for the next two records. Every song is credited to all four members.

The album is 36 minutes and six songs, and "Anisette" alone takes up nearly a quarter of it.

years.h: Mueller and Jason Noble start Shipping News while June of 44 is still going
years.p: Mueller and his Rodan bandmate [[Jason Noble|1a30edd1-b7ee-4d9f-ae1c-af8cd4759718]] form [[Shipping News|d6ed84da-0414-4c44-ace7-ae491ce7d999]] with drummer Kyle Crabtree. Its debut Save Everything came out on Quarterstick in 1997.
years.xp: Shipping News would outlast June of 44, with four albums on Quarterstick between 1997 and 2005. Noble was diagnosed with synovial sarcoma in 2009 and died on August 4, 2012, at 40, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller
years.h: The Anatomy of Sharks EP keeps the ocean theme going
years.p: An EP released between Tropics and Meridians and Four Great Points.
years.xp: The sea imagery runs through the first three albums and the band's titles, and Mueller says it was mostly his idea.

eras.title: Dub, strings and a fifteen-minute closer
eras.text: The band that started as four guitars and drums adds violin, electronics, organ and tube radio. It ends with an album's worth of ideas and not enough time to finish them.

q: Each subsequent record was increasingly more collaborative.
years.src: Wikipedia: Four Great Points · Leo Weekly: A conversation with Jeff Mueller of June of 44
years.h: Four Great Points takes a year and two studios
years.p: Recorded between August 1996 and August 1997 at Electrical Audio in Chicago and Sound Techniques in Boston, with Weston producing.
years.xp:
Julie Liu adds violin and Bundy K. Brown of [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]] adds electronics, and Erskine plays trumpet. Pitchfork gave it a 9.0, and the Chicago Reader called it a hypnotic blend of rock, dub, ambient and orchestral pop.

Mueller says each record after the first got more collaborative, which is why the instrumentation gets more mixed up.

years.p: Footage of the four-piece playing "Sharks and Sailors" on stage in 1998, the year of Four Great Points.

years.src: Discogs: June Of 44 - In The Fishtank
years.h: Two days in a Dutch studio, six songs, an old organ and a tube radio
years.p: Konkurrent's In the Fishtank series gives June of 44 its sixth slot, recorded during their European tour.
years.xp: The liner notes call it the missing link between Four Great Points and Anahata. The session uses an old organ and a tube radio set, and the six tracks include "Henry's Revenge" and "Every Free Day a Good Day". Konkurrent was the Dutch label behind the series.

years.src: Wikipedia: Anahata (album) · Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years · Wikipedia: June of 44
years.h: Anahata closes on "Peel Away Velleity", 15 minutes long
years.p: Eight songs, about 50 minutes, recorded in January 1999 at Electrical Audio, with Weston again.
years.xp:
Reviews split: Exclaim! called it the band's most satisfying outing to date, while CMJ found the unison shouting a drag. Pitchfork gave it 7.8. Sources disagree on the label, and Wikipedia's band page lists it as Konkurrent.

Twenty years later Mueller would say the sessions were tough and that many of the songs felt underdeveloped.

years.src: Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years · Leo Weekly: A conversation with Jeff Mueller of June of 44 · Wikipedia: June of 44 · Wikipedia: Jeff Mueller · Wikipedia: Hoover (band)
years.h: Final show of the first run, in November 1999
years.p: The four scatter into their side projects: Mueller to Shipping News, Erskine to Abilene, Scharin to HiM, Meadows to Everlasting the Way, later Letter E.
years.xp: Mueller says the side projects did not cause the split, only that the band ended. He released a solo album, Fold and Perish, that year on Monitor. Scharin's HiM had started in 1995, and Erskine had played in the Crownhate Ruin alongside Hoover.

eras.title: A birthday party in Sicily
eras.text: A phone call from Catania is enough to end a nineteen-year hiatus, and a new record turns out to be an old one.

q: We just felt like it had to happen.
years.src: Stereogum: June Of 44 Reunite For First Shows In 19 Years · Leo Weekly: A conversation with Jeff Mueller of June of 44 · Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years
years.h: Uzeda calls, and June of 44 plays for the first time in 19 years
years.p: The Sicilian band [[Uzeda|9cb56cf1-bd4a-4d59-8ecb-dc412f595dd3]] asks them to play its 30th anniversary in Catania, and the four say yes. Catania on May 25 and 26, then Turin, Bologna and Rome.
years.xp:
The Italian run, as Stereogum listed it, was Catania on May 25 and 26, Turin on May 28, Bologna on May 29 and Rome on May 30. Mueller says that when Uzeda's Agostino called, it just felt like it had to happen.

The band kept playing through 2018 and 2019, including Bay Area dates in fall 2019 before the recording sessions for the next record.

years.big: Many of the songs felt underdeveloped.
years.src: Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years · POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller · Wikipedia: June of 44
years.h: Revisionist re-records and remixes the old songs
years.p: Mueller on the Anahata sessions, in explaining why Revisionist: Adaptations & Future Histories in the Time of Love and Survival exists. The band announced it in July.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone reported the album was recorded in California in 2019. Mueller said the original session had been tough, and the new project was a chance to think through material the band had never given itself time to consider.

He also said he wanted to present the songs as they were written, not necessarily as they were played in the 1990s.

eras.title: Tokyo, and two guitars
eras.text: The reunion goes global, then gets a live record, and Mueller and Meadows start a duo.

years.src: POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller · Wikipedia: June of 44
years.h: Japan and Australia, with a Tokyo show taped
years.p: In 2023 the band toured Japan and Australia, with sold-out shows. The March 9 gig at Club Fever in Tokyo was recorded.
years.xp: Mueller describes the recent shows as more ceremony and celebration than youthful aggression, and says the reunion was about understanding the material more than replicating the 1990s.

years.h: Mueller and Meadows debut Flowting Clowds
years.p: Meadows and Mueller start a duo, Flowting Clowds, with a first single in November 2025 and shows across the northern U.S.

years.h: Live in Tokyo announced, taped at Club Fever in 2023
years.p: A live album recorded March 9, 2023 at Club Fever, announced on Bandcamp in January 2026.
